The injected geodesic disk range gives F(r)=pi*r^2/(LH) for r<min(L,H)/2. Both min terms reach (L^2+H^2)/4 exactly when A=B=L/2,V=H/2, proving the support diameter. With alpha=L/2−A,beta=L/2−B,delta=V−H/2, the rescaled inequalities for s=rho^2−r^2 are 0<u<(1+Hz)/L,0<w<(1−Hz)/L, |z|<1/H; the density is 4/(L^2 H). The integral (4/(L^4 H))*integral_{−1/H}^{1/H}(1−H^2 z^2)dz equals 16/(3L^4 H^2), a full all-aspect ratio dominated-convergence proof. Small-ball area LH and endpoint coefficient reconstruct L and H uniquely. Independent pointwise deck-reduction checks and rescaled numerical quadrature for (L,H)=(1,2),(2,1),(3,2) found near-tail ratios 1.009102,1.006044,1.007620 at small positive s; these only corroborate the proved limit.
